title: feat(types): refuse the function-slot mirror keys by name (objectui#7759 group E)
body:
Part of #7759: group E (FUNCTION-SLOT) only. The card stays open for groups C and D.

Clause-②: yes (the mirror's accept set narrows on a published surface; an isolated at-tier contract review happens before enqueue)

## What changed

Ruling 5617465269 (「E 组按 #6124 直接派」) is applied to the four non-`on*` keys that the zod mirrors still declared as a bare `z.function()`. Each key now uses the objectui#6124 `handlerKeyRefusal()` arm. I measured each key's disposition from its read sites on `origin/main` `d16d0e977`:

| key | disposition | read-site evidence | TS twin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TableColumnSchema.cell` | runtime-slot | `data-table.tsx` calls `col.cell(cellValue, row)`, and `ObjectGrid.tsx` / `VirtualGrid.tsx` call it the same way | keeps its function type |
| `DataTableSchema.renderCellEditor` | runtime-slot | `data-table.tsx` reads `schema.renderCellEditor` and calls it, and `ObjectGrid` supplies it | keeps its function type |
| `FieldConstraintsSchema.validate` | runtime-slot | the form renderer spreads `validation` into react-hook-form `rules` and keeps a supplied `validate` function running next to its own `required` entry | keeps its function type |
| `FieldConditionSchema.custom` | retired | `legacyConditionToCel` in `form.tsx` reads `field` / `equals` / `notEquals` / `in` and never `custom`. `FieldCondition` has no other importer, and `evaluateCondition` in `@object-ui/fields` does not read `custom` either | `custom?: never` |

None of the five pairs appears in `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS`, and `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 declares none of these keys. That makes them objectui-owned keys, which ruling 5617465269 principle 2 covers (the read site is the source of truth). I also re-checked the #6124 stop condition: the only runtime `safeParse` doors into these mirrors are the CLI file validators (`safeValidateSchema`), and they only ever parse JSON/YAML files, so no legitimate function value goes through `safeParse`.

## Ledger movement (measured with `tsc`, not assumed)

- **`WiderThanDeclared` loses 8 rows**, not 5. The five dispatched keys cleared as expected, and `FormFieldSchema::validation` cleared as the PM predicted. Two more cleared on their own: `DataTableSchema::columns`, which was filed as group F, and `FormSchema::fields`, which was filed as group D. Both read wider only because of the function arm nested under them. After this change, `WiderOf` resolves to `never` for DataTable, TableColumn, FieldConstraints, FieldCondition and FormField, and to `layout | mode` for FormSchema. These rows left because the ledger ratchet requires it. No group D or F ruling was applied.
- **`KnownDrift` gains 3 entries / 5 keys**, all in the narrower direction, with the same runtime-slot shape as the #6124 keys. The new entries are `TableColumnSchema.cell`, `FieldConstraintsSchema.validate` and `FormFieldSchema.validation` (which inherits `validate`). `DataTableSchema` gains `renderCellEditor`, plus `columns`, which inherits `cell`. `custom` is `never` on both faces and measures clean.
- I updated the header figures and added their history sentences. The pins that read them are green.

## Tension with #6124 Q4 → B, stated, not quietly settled

The #6124 ruling Q4 → B said 「`cell`/`custom`/`validate` 留镜像原样」, and `handler-keys-json-refusal-6124.test.ts` pinned that the four sites stay as they are. Ruling 5617465269 is later and names group E for #6124 treatment, so this PR reads it as extending the #6124 arm to these keys. I rewrote that pin to assert zero remaining sites, gave it a synthetic positive control, and pointed it at the new pin. Q4's actual blocker was that `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` cannot hold non-`on*` keys. That blocker does not apply here: the keys stay mirrored, and `KnownDrift` has no callback-shape restriction.

## Tests (every run at head `64ebcedb3`, after merging `origin/main`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/`: `Test Files 215 passed (215)`, `Tests 4956 passed (4956)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` + examples + `tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0.
- Downstream, after building the closure (`--filter '@object-ui/plugin-form^...' '@object-ui/plugin-grid^...' '@object-ui/components^...' '@object-ui/react^...' run build`): `type-check` on types, react, components, plugin-form and plugin-grid all reported Done, exit 0. This ran before the merge. The merge brought in no change to these files.
- Gates: `check-changeset-presence`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:control-bytes`, `check-changeset-no-major`. All exit 0.
- eslint (`--no-inline-config`) on the 9 changed `.ts` files: 0 errors. The 41 warnings are all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` hits on lines this PR does not add.
- **New pin** `function-slot-keys-json-refusal-7759.test.ts` covers three things. For each key it checks that the key is still declared on `.shape` and carries the #6124 guidance, that JSON values and live functions are refused with `code: custom` at the key's own path, and that the object parses green without the key. It checks refusal at the nested paths (`validation.validate`, `condition.custom`, `columns.0.cell`). It also runs type-level `KeepsFunction` on the three runtime slots and `RetiredIsNever` on `custom`.
- **Reverse verification**, both on committed state via `ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored to blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty:
  1. Reverting `validate` to `z.function()` turned 9 tests red, which were exactly the `validate` rows plus both census pins.
  2. Reverting `FieldCondition.custom` to a function type turned `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` red twice: TS2344 on the new pin's `RetiredIsNever` line, and the parity ledger's `LedgerMismatch`.
- Cross-package check: a probe in `@object-ui/components` assigned an arrow function to `FieldCondition.custom` and got TS2322 against the rebuilt `dist` (`form.d.ts` carries `custom?: never`). I then removed the probe.

## Acceptance notes

- `handlerKeyRefusal()` ends every message with the remedy text written for `on*` handlers (write a node type such as `toast` or `action:button`). For `cell`, `validate` and `renderCellEditor` that remedy fits poorly. The key-specific pointer lives in the TS JSDoc and the site comments. I left the shared helper unchanged, as the dispatch asked. A per-site remedy parameter would be a follow-up if someone wants it.
- Two changesets pending in the same release still describe these keys as `z.function()`: the 6124 one and the 7188 one. This PR's changeset says it supersedes those statements. I did not edit either pending changeset.
- Docs: I removed `custom` from the legacy matcher row in `packages/plugin-form/README.md` and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-form.mdx`, which the claim's file surface did not list. Both docs already describe `validate` as available to TypeScript-authored schemas only.
- The first commit's trailer names the model. Later commits use a model-free trailer. History is not rewritten.
